papers.title_in_file: A Knowledge Compilation Map for Quantum Information
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Sections 1, 5 overview, 7 Discussion; theorem statements in Sections 3 to 5; appendix proofs not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: An analytical comparison of the succinctness, tractability and rapidity of MPS, decision diagram and RBM representations of quantum states.

assertions.value: The authors report that the succinctness of MPS, RBM and LIMDD is incomparable, and that MPS is strictly more succinct than SLDD.
quotes: we find that the succinctness of MPS, RBM and LIMDD are incomparable.
We also find that MPS is strictly more succinct than SLDD

assertions.value: The authors prove that computing fidelity and inner product in RBM and LIMDD is intractable, assuming the exponential time hypothesis.
quotes: Finally, we prove that computing fidelity and inner product in RBM and LIMDD is intractable assuming the exponential time hypothesis.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 3 and Lemma 31 / Corollary 37 in the appendix

assertions.value: The authors state that more research is needed to compare the relative performance of these data structures on the various application domains in practice.
quotes: Therefore, more research is needed to compare the relative performance of these data structures on the various application domains in practice.
assertions.certainty_reason: Sec. 7 states the scope limit: the comparison is analytical

papers.title_in_file: Geodesics of Quantum Feature Maps on the Space of Quantum Operators
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Discussion (Summary and Future Directions), Lemma 58 region; derivations not checked line by line.
papers.what_it_is: A mathematical paper deriving Riemannian geometry (metric, curvature, volume forms, harmonic maps) for the range of Hamiltonian quantum feature maps in the special unitary group.

assertions.value: The author states that the paper derives analytic formulas for curvature, volume forms and harmonic maps for a broad class of Hamiltonian quantum feature maps.
quotes: we derive analytic and, consequently, computational formulas for fundamental geometric measurements, including curvature, volume forms, and harmonic maps
assertions.certainty_reason: Derivations in Secs. II to IV (analytic, no experiment)

assertions.value: The paper states that a geodesic on the embedded manifold is also a geodesic on the range of the quantum feature map.
quotes: One of the more important results shows that geodesic on the embedded manifold is also the geodesic on the range of the quantum feature map.
assertions.certainty_reason: Sec. V.1 summarizes the proved result

assertions.value: The author states that a connection between the geometric structure of an encoding scheme and model performance is posited, not established in this paper.
quotes: In fact, it is posited that there is a connection between the geometric structure of an encoding scheme and the performance of a quantum-based statistical model.
assertions.certainty_reason: Sec. V.2 marks this link as posited

papers.title_in_file: Extreme Events of Quantum Walks on Graphs
papers.partial_detail: Main text (abstract, introduction, results, summary); supplementary information not in the file.
papers.what_it_is: A physics letter on extreme events in discrete-time quantum walks on ring and scale-free graphs, compared with classical random walks.

assertions.value: The authors report that extreme event probability for quantum walks on a scale-free graph is larger for small degree nodes than for hubs, as it is for classical random walks.
quotes: For both classical and quantum walks, the extreme event probability is larger for small degree nodes compared to hubs on the graph.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation on one graph family

assertions.value: The authors state that they obtain a quantum version of the flux-fluctuation relation, and that the derivation relies on a non-degenerate eigenspectrum of the walk operator.
quotes: Firstly, we obtain quantum version of flux-fluctuation relation and use this to define to extreme events on vertices of a graph as exceedences above the mean flux.
non-degeneracy of eigenspectrum of U guarantees that the second term has a vanishing contribution
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytic argument with an assumption, checked by simulation on one setup

assertions.value: The authors state that when the eigenvalues of the walk operator are degenerate, the quantum walk strongly deviates from the classical walk.
quotes: Then, the DTQW strongly deviates from the classical walk.

papers.title_in_file: Data reconstruction based on quantum neural networks
papers.what_it_is: Proposes QNN and quantum autoencoder frameworks for image super-resolution style data reconstruction, simulated on small MNIST digits.

assertions.value: The authors report that in simulation the QNN with Circuit 2 reaches fidelities close to the classical SRCNN, with a much smaller number of parameters.
quotes: Besides, fidelities of the QNN with Circuit 2 are close to the classical SRCNN, which means QNNs can achieve nearly the same effect for image super-resolution as CNN but with much less number of parameters.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single small simulation; the figures are in Table 1 only

assertions.value: The authors state that the experiments use small MNIST digit sets of 50 training images and 30 test images each.
quotes: where each set contains 50 images for training and 30 images for testing.

assertions.value: The authors state that the choice of circuit structure greatly affects the QNN and QAE reconstruction result.
quotes: the selection of circuit structures (or ansatz) greatly affects the result of QNN and QAE for our data reconstruction task.

papers.title_in_file: Variational data encoding and correlations in quantum-enhanced machine learning
papers.what_it_is: Introduces a trainable (variational) data encoding for quantum regression and simulates the effect of entanglement and local noise.

assertions.value: The authors report that in simulation their variational quantum regression algorithms, even with a limited number of qubits and shallow circuit depth, closely approximate all the tested functions.
quotes: demonstrate that VQRAs, even with a limited number of qubits and shallow circuit depth, are capable of closely approximating all the tested functions.

assertions.value: The authors report that circuit configurations allowing greater quantum correlations showed relatively better resilience to local noise in simulation.
quotes: configurations allowing for greater quantum correlations demonstrated relatively better resilience to noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated symmetric depolarizing noise on small circuits

assertions.value: The authors state that they could not quantitatively assess the role of quantum correlations because no universally accepted metric for multi-body quantum correlations exists.
quotes: However, our study faced challenges in quantitatively assessing the role of quantum correlations due to the absence of a universally accepted metric for multi-body quantum correlations.

papers.title_in_file: Time series prediction of open quantum system dynamics
papers.what_it_is: A classical Transformer model is trained to forecast the dynamics of a single-qubit open quantum system.

assertions.value: The authors report that for long-term prediction the fidelity between predicted and exact density matrices exceeds 0.96 for all tested cases.
quotes: From Fig. 4, the fidelity exceeds 0.96 for all cases, indicating the accuracy prediction ability of our trained model.

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper considers only a simple single-qubit system and that the method might lose effectiveness for multi-qubit systems.
quotes: Additionally, in this paper we only consider a simple single-qubit system.
For multiqubit systems, our method might lose its effectiveness
assertions.certainty_reason: Sec. V states the scope limit

assertions.value: The authors report that cumulative prediction error grows as the number of prediction steps increases.
quotes: We can also see that as the number of prediction steps increases, the cumulative prediction error also increases as expected.
assertions.certainty_reason: Observed in the paper's own simulation

papers.title_in_file: Limitations of Amplitude Encoding on Quantum Classification
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sec. III A statement of Theorem 1 and discussion, Conclusion; appendix proofs and numerical sections not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: Proves a loss-barrier lower bound for quantum classifiers when encoded class-average states are similar, and shows amplitude encoding meets that condition under data assumptions.

assertions.value: The paper proves that if the encoded class-average states are similar across classes, the cross-entropy loss has a lower bound close to ln K, for any circuit and optimizer.
quotes: Theorem 1 clearly shows that if the expectations of encoded quantum states are similar across different classes
has a lower bound close to ln K.

assertions.value: The authors prove that under some broad data assumptions the average of amplitude-encoded states concentrates towards a specific state.
quotes: we prove that under some broad and typical data assumptions, the average of encoded quantum states via amplitude encoding tends to concentrate towards a specific state.

assertions.value: The authors report from numerical simulations that with amplitude encoding the training error may increase as the amount of training data increases.
quotes: as the amount of training data increases, the training error may increase rather than decrease

assertions.value: The authors state that they focus on the variational-encoding paradigm, where data encoding and the variational circuit are separated.
quotes: In this work we focus on the variational-encoding paradigm.

papers.what_it_is: Proposes an adaptive Hamiltonian learning circuit and a noise-resistant QNN, tested in Paddle Quantum simulation under amplitude damping noise.

assertions.value: The author reports that RQNN reached an accuracy of 98.00 % on a non-linear discrete data classification under amplitude damping noise, higher than the compared quantum neural network.
quotes: achieve high classification accuracy on the same non-linear discrete data classification under the impact of amplitude damping noise, with an accuracy of 98.00 %, which is higher than the quantum neural network [20].
assertions.reader_inference: Sec. 5 gives 98.00% as the training-set accuracy; the test-set figure is in Table 2 only.

assertions.value: The author states that the dataset has 450 elements, 300 for training and 150 for testing, and that the models run 100 iterations on 4 qubits.
quotes: The overall dataset consists of 450 elements, with 300 elements in the training set and 150 elements in the test set.
run 100 iterations. The number of quantum qubits that are used is 4.

assertions.value: The author states that the experiments on Paddle Quantum demonstrate accurate classification results on NISQ devices.
quotes: Finally, the experiments on Paddle Quantum demonstrate that RQNN can simulate the mathematical function and get accurate classification results on NISQ devices.
